newsitem.title: BELGIUM: World steel output jump 7.3 percent in May yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: World steel output jump 7.3 percent in May yr/yr.

text.p: World steel output rose 7.3 percent to 66.9 million tonnes in May compared with the same month last year, boosted by strong figures in Asia, western Europe, Brazil and Poland, the International Iron and Steel Institute (IISI) said on Thursday.
For the first five months of 1997, crude steel production rose 5.4 percent to 319.3 million tonnes year-on-year in the 66 countries covered in the monthly survey.
In May, steel production continued on an upward trend in Asia with output rising 11.1 percent to 25.3 million tonnes -- more than a third of total world production.
Production in China rose 10.3 percent to 9.1 million tonnes while the Japanese figure was 9.5 percent higher at 9.2 million tonnes.

Total Eastern European output rose seven percent to 2.8 million tonnes, helped by a jump of 21.6 percent to 1.1 million tonnes in Poland. However, output in the former Soviet Union declined by 3.1 percent to 6.7 million tonnes.
Western Europe's output firmed eight percent to 15.2 million tonnes.

Production in Brazil soared 15 percent to 2.2 million tonnes while overall production in South America rose 8.6 percent to 3.1 million tonnes. North American output rose 7.1 percent to 11.2 million tonnes.
